name: Census completeness (how many early orders are still unseen)
role: Compares the independent printed lists of 1789-1899 orders and estimates, with stated bias, how many orders none of them has seen.
inputs: land-office and military-reservation books fetched by early-orders-hunt
outputs: ESTIMATES.json and REPORT.md (completeness claim in defensible form)

results.text: Run 2026-10-22T18:25:02Z: 3,442 dated mentions from 18 lists; 7,427 cross-list matches (5,902 blind date+word, 1,195 blind year+two words, 330 citation links); 5,002 same-date pairs left unmatched; 1,420 distinct unnumbered orders dated 1789-1899 observed (56 numbered clusters set aside). Estimated missed by the lists: about 129.1 (every same-date pair treated as one order) to 295.7 (strict matching); both are lower bounds.
First local run: 2,553 mentions from 11 lists; 1,394 distinct unnumbered orders observed; 1801-1861 total estimated 316 (95% CI 269-362), 1862-1899 estimated 1,729 (1,634-1,825).

history.text: Job added to estimate early orders the lists have not found.
Re-run on 18 lists (up from 11) with later hunt books; estimates moved accordingly. Only the two runs above are recorded; no further iteration log.

caveats: Population-level estimates only: admits no order, assigns no date, merges no identity, changes no count or status (README:91-92).
Lord drew on the same books, so every estimate under-states the undiscovered remainder (README:31-35).
Orders that never reached a printed compilation are invisible; the random archival audit that would measure them is a step no job can do (README:52-56).
Clark reads this job's output folder (jobs/clark-discovery/needs.txt:4); the handoff is for dated-unnumbered leads, not identities.

name: Census candidates (early LOC item register)
role: Joins the early-ranger outputs to Library of Congress item IDs and lists them as candidate early orders, never as admitted orders.

results.text: Run 2026-10-22T15:18:55Z: 67 distinct LOC item-ID candidates; 10 items with a LOC XML transcript; 3 items with saved original pages (10 pages referenced); 5 uncrosswalked historical representations; 1,023 Lord index appearances (unauthenticated); 812 Lord 19th-century gap rows; 0 newly admitted EOs; 0 independent human certifications.

history.text: Early-census candidate register added.
Dependency ordering on the six early-ranger producers wired and tested.

caveats: Cannot admit an order, change a status or issue human approval; a reviewer must separately authenticate physical content, issuer capacity, duplicates, legal inclusion and chronology (README:10).
Matches by exact LOC item ID only; date-only or similar-title matches never identify an instrument (README:3).
Its 10 transcripts and 3 saved-page items come from the earlier successful ranger state; the ranger's later same-day re-run at PIN shows 0 metadata retrieved (see early-ranger node).

name: Clark (orders the project cannot yet identify)

namesake.text: William Clark, as named in the project's tool catalog; paired with Lewis as the 'Corps of Discovery' jobs

role: Looks for orders the project knows only by number or not at all (gaps in the numbering, numbers cited in texts) and passes any identity clues to Lewis.
inputs: saved order texts and OFR disposition notes
APP index, OFR catalog, WPA list, ProQuest link list
open-web search (list pages and targeted queries)

results.text: Run 2026-10-29T07:14:51Z: 46 number gaps (26 strong, 8 cited, 12 number-only; highest numbered order 14435); 145 distinct cited-but-unknown ids, of which 60 plausible; 61 identity-unknown census orders, 48 of them number-only; 226 dated-unnumbered rows (127 distinct dates); 55 handoff rows to Lewis. No identities admitted.

history.text: First offline version: 46 number gaps (22 of them the June 1932 run EO 5853-5879); 26 plausible cited-but-unknown ids from 27,017 texts and 5,063 OFR notes; 3,432 census orders known by number only; 414 dated unnumbered references.
Taken online: open-web engine search and list-page harvest added.
Kean finding: one owner-ruling file selected 14 jobs including Clark's hour-long web search; web searches now run in full only on schedule or when their own inputs change.

caveats: Leads only: nothing enters the census, changes a readiness count or authenticates an identity (README:60-65).
A number gap is a lead for census intake, not an entry; the June 1932 gap is probably an ingestion miss but only a person checking the identity layer can say so (README:62-65).
Counts across dates (3,432 number-only on 2026-10-21 vs 61 identity-unknown on 2026-10-29) are not shown by the repo to be the same measure; do not read them as progress.

name: Domesday register (one row per known order)

namesake.text: The 1086 Domesday survey, which records what is held, not what is true
namesake.evidence: jobs/domesday-register/register.py:1,10; jobs/domesday-register/README.md:16; TOOLS.csv row Domesday register

role: Keeps one table of every order in the 14,972-order census and what the project holds for it, refreshed daily.

results.text: Run 2026-10-29T07:27:19Z: 14,972 orders; best_held label counts: official_original_counted 6,968 (register's raw label; includes working transcriptions, not all official originals), official_found_page_check_pending 285, archival_replica_scan 2,750, transcription_only 4,879, nothing 90; 14,882 with any text file; 56 candidate numbers not in the census (37 strong, 9 cited, 6 weak, 4 unrated).
Digest comparison against 2026-10-22: with_any_text_file 11,517 to 14,882; with_title 10,139 to 14,885.

history.text: Register added: 6,872 originals counted, 4,354 transcription-only, 3,449 nothing held; 54 candidates not in the census (old catalog row).
Source jobs connected and offline draft verification enforced.

caveats: Records what is held, not what is true: no identity, custody grade, readiness count or legal status changes here (README:16-18; SUMMARY.json what_this_is_not).
The census file stays the only universe and the readiness tracker the only count.
The 'official_original_counted' label counts a text step as done and includes working transcriptions; do not read it as 6,968 official originals.
Candidates not in the register are leads for census intake, never register rows (README:10-14).

name: Domesday tool audit (2026-10-20)

namesake.text: The 1086 survey that recorded what every holding was worth

role: A one-time audit by an agent of what each tool had measurably contributed to the ready-for-review count as of 20 October.
outputs: audit memo with three tool groups and a recommendation

results.text: At that date 225 of 14,972 orders were ready for human review, all via agent-written claim batches (129 from 1989 Codification families, 68 Lambertini I-III, 9 Lamm, 6 Rastell, 5 X1 pilot, 3 Bowditch Y2, 5 other); the meta-tools (Junto, Llull, Polya, NEYMAN, NORTON, Hamilton, Valla, Mountweazel) had $0 verified savings. Old count, not current.

Found that acquisition jobs hathi-gpo-orders, numbered-early-orders, early-orders-hunt, wikisource-texts and the early-ranger family had output the tracker never read; recommendation was to fix and wire existing tools and build no new ones.

history.text: Written while merging PRs #38, #40, #42-#45.
Source jobs were then connected to the tracker.

caveats: Historical snapshot: the 225 and every other count in it are superseded by the current published readiness.
Cost figures marked 'est.' in the memo are agent estimates, not measurements.
Different from the Domesday register (the live table); catalog keeps them as separate rows.

name: Early-order ranger (1789-1861 manuscript leads, 1862-1906 gap screens)
role: A chain of bounded jobs that search Library of Congress catalogs for early manuscript candidates, triage them, fetch item metadata, transcripts and page images, and screen 1862-1906 year gaps.
inputs: LOC public JSON service and Internet Archive metadata

results.text: Final committed re-run (18:20 UTC): scout 28 live responses preserved, 35 distinct item links, 0 pre-1862 executive orders authenticated, 4 LOC request failures; triage 65 candidates, 6 directive-title leads; original-items 21 planned, 0 metadata retrieved (4 failed, 17 skipped after provider failures); transcriptions 0 XML links, 0 preserved. Earlier same-day state: 20 of 21 item metadata retrieved (16:13 UTC) and 10 XML transcripts with 10,514 words.

Full-pages: 3 target items, 10 original master JPEG pages acquired (3,406,378 bytes), page counts unchanged. 1862-1906 screen: 611 proxy orders in 32 years vs 812 unverified Lord OCR date markers; 180 search routes planned; 0 historical EOs authenticated.

One-off jobs: facsimiles pilot 14 files for 7 items (2,694,849 bytes); workbench 21 source items, 9 with transcriptions; year-reconcile found Stage 15 shows 611 and Stage 17 shows 617 proxy orders in 1862-1906 (18 ids changed).

history.text: Variable-plan repair after run 39666192712 failed on a fixed 23-response assertion; offline replay passed 11 new tests; independent swarm review found no blocking issue and a reporting fix.
Facsimile, full-page, workbench and year-reconcile jobs added.
Ranger chain scout to reparse to triage to original-items to transcriptions/full-pages to census-candidates ordered in after.txt files.

caveats: Discovery only: no catalog result is authenticated as a presidential executive order, and a failed or empty search does not prove absence (SCOUT_SUMMARY.json).

The last committed original-items and transcriptions outputs are a provider-failure re-run (0 retrieved), later than the successful 20-of-21 state census-candidates used; the repo does not show a successful re-run after it.
early-ranger-workbench, -year-reconcile and -facsimiles are one-off 2026-10-17/21 jobs with no downstream consumer found in after.txt.
Nothing here admits an order, assigns legal status or creates a human-certified lifecycle.

name: Early orders hunt (printed texts of 1789-1899 orders)
role: Reads the book citations in Lord's 1943 list, fetches those printed books from the Internet Archive and cuts out the page where each early order is printed.
inputs: Lord list entries (1,158) and OCR date markers (1,023)
Internet Archive page OCR of GLO, MR, Richardson volumes
outputs: texts/ passage slices with page, hash and grade

results.text: Run 2026-10-22T18:24:59Z (184.9 s): 1,994 leads (320 before 1862); 6,744 citations parsed; 6,261 citations resolved against held books, 3,240 of them graded page_date_and_subject, 2,096 book_not_held; 1,027 leads with a text cut (146 before 1862); 4,082 text slices written; 24 live LOC routes prepared, 0 searched.
First live run from the owner's PC (6 books): 950 leads got a text, 125 of them before 1862; every fetched book matched the Archive's sha1; 12 LOC searches for 1789-1790 leads.

history.text: Job added to fetch the printed texts of 1789-1899 orders Lord cites.
Domesday audit listed it among acquisition jobs whose output the tracker never read; connection followed on 2026-10-21.

caveats: A printed compilation is a transcription lead for the original_text step, never the signed original (README:63-69).
A page hit is not an identity; signer, capacity and inclusion stay with the reviewer.
Not a measure of orders found: a slice must be read against the scan (README:94). A search with no results proves nothing.
catalog_tool is a shared row covering five jobs; only early-orders-hunt, numbered-early-orders and app-executive-orders are in this file.

name: American Presidency Project harvest
role: Collects the American Presidency Project's executive-order index and page texts, live at a polite pace and from web-archive captures.
inputs: Common Crawl and Wayback Machine captures
outputs: DOCUMENTS.jsonl and MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl with page hashes

results.text: STATE.json: 10,840 documents indexed (9,949 distinct instrument ids, 890 unnumbered); 792 live pages saved, 0 failed; 10,317 saved from archive captures; complete. Audit of every 50th capture: 205 of 205 compared texts agree with the live page (page bytes differ, site chrome only).

history.text: Polite live harvester, full index and statistics table; then archive lane (Common Crawl/Wayback) and live-lane audit sample.
516 numbered orders were saved only from the live site (hash kept, bytes not); archive-only backfill added as Poggio and a host guard stops the lane ever requesting APP.
Archive lane now retries a response the archive server cuts short.

caveats: An APP page is an editorial transcription, not a signed original or an identity authentication; texts stay acceptable_as_original=false.
No job.py: explicit local invocation only, so a runner and a PC never crawl APP at once (README.txt:3-5); not run on a schedule.
APP statistics are editorial counts and a comparison source, not a census finding.
catalog_tool is a shared row covering five jobs; this node is only one of them.

name: APP transcriptions (shape converter)
role: Re-packages the archive-captured APP texts into the file shapes the dossier builder and later-events reader can see.

results.text: Run 2026-10-19T18:16:04Z: 9,387 archive-lane fragments written; 9,902 source records written (9,871 in the census, 31 not); 910 records refused as not exactly one order.

history.text: Added so about 9,400 archive-lane texts become visible to claim-kit and later-events; tracker reads APP as a lead only.

caveats: Every record stays mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original=false; counted as a lead (ONLY_COMPILED_TRANSCRIPTION_FOUND), not an original (README:19-26).
Fetches nothing and edits nothing upstream; must be re-run by hand when app-executive-orders changes (README:31-32).
No re-run recorded after 2026-10-19 at PIN, so Poggio's 2026-10-29 captures are not shown as folded in.

name: APP footnote leads
role: Splits the editorial footnote under each APP order page into typed sentences, such as Federal Register publication notes and 'amended by' notes.
outputs: EDGES.csv (acting order to this order, lead-only)

results.text: Run 2026-10-19T18:16:00Z: 792 live and 10,270 archive pages read; 1,994 distinct footnotes; sentence rows: 1,211 fr_citation, 48 not_published, 3 amended_by, 0 revoked_by, 0 superseded_by, 1,415 other; 4 later-order edges (all amendment).

history.text: Job added.

caveats: Footnotes are editorial notes on a secondary transcription; a row is a lead, never an ending, effective date, status finding or proof of publication (README:38-42).
Edges are flagged app_editorial_note_not_ofr;lead_only_never_an_ending.
Why a separate job: it cannot go into later-events without misattributing the note's source (README:29-36).

name: Numbered early orders (printed texts of orders 1-5075)
role: Searches government printed books page by page for the texts of 3,324 undecided numbered orders from 1862-1929.
inputs: data/TARGETS.csv (3,324 orders from census gap list and WPA 1944 numbered list)

results.text: Run 2026-10-19T00:30:59Z: 184 of 3,324 targets got a text (197 texts): 41 from books already held, 143 from newly fetched books (Civil Service reports 95, Kappler IV 26, Official U.S. Bulletin 17, Panama Canal 1921 6); 3,140 still without text; 30 requests, 1 fetch failure.

history.text: Job added, then extended with Civil Service reports, Kappler III and Panama 1921.
Known false positive recorded: EO 860 matched on a later order quoting it.

caveats: A printed copy is never the signed original; a date-and-subject hit is a machine match to confirm against the scan (README:32-34).
Nothing here admits an order, decides a status or authenticates a text.
Most of the remaining 3,140 are minor 1908-29 orders; the Internet Archive holds only four 1908-29 Civil Service years and HathiTrust is not fetched (README:47-50).
catalog_tool is a shared row covering five jobs; this node is only one of them.

name: Library survey (PDF reading pilot)
role: A one-time trial of PDF text-extraction, OCR and citation-finding libraries on preserved official-source PDFs.
inputs: retained Stage 18 and Stage 21 official-source PDFs (20)

results.text: Run 2026-10-17: 22 PDFs, 28 pages; pdfplumber returned longer text than pypdf on 28 of 28 pages (length, not accuracy); OCRmyPDF read 2 of 2 printed historical images (7,118 characters); eyecite found 54 reporter-citation leads; 0 legal statuses changed; no accuracy scoring.

history.text: Added with the early-census register and Opus plan; then exercised OCRmyPDF on two printed images.
Kean finding: closest thing to an OCR comparison, but handwriting was never tested and no error rate exists.

caveats: A pilot; the README says to adopt into fr-originals or source-ladder only after measured recoverability checks, and no adoption is recorded here (README:7).
Citation matches are leads, not evidence an order is still operative.
Longer extracted text is not shown to be more accurate text.

name: Corpus excavator (profiler and source-pass planner)
role: Profiles every census order against the tracker to list what work remains, ranks a small source-fetch plan, and lists historical witnesses and gaps outside the census.

results.text: Run 2026-10-29T07:15:06Z: its tracker snapshot then showed 14,972 identities, 11,569 undecided, 395 ready (older than the published 498); ranked 12-request source pass has readiness ceiling 2, demonstrated gain before execution 0; 115 discovery records outside the census (67 catalog candidates, 46 numbered-series gaps, 2 unnumbered editorial witnesses), 0 authenticated identities.

history.text: Source-priority pilot: top twelve requests offered 163 overlapping open-step memberships and a ceiling of one new-ready order, which failed source/legal audit; effort shifted to status-history.
Fingerprinted readiness-aware source plans added; pilot frozen.
Domesday audit listed it with 'demonstrated gain 0'; NEYMAN extension added planning-only closures.

caveats: Never fetches and never establishes a lifecycle conclusion; readiness ceilings are machine steps, not accepted outcomes (README:3, 19).
Profile groups overlap; use ORDER_FRONTIER for disjoint counts. Retrieval failure never means search exhaustion.
The source-ladder handoff is manual (JOB_PLAN_FILE=...), not automatic (README:9-13).
Different from the research/excavator campaign folders (agent claim runs); only the 2026-10-18 report is listed here.

name: Poggio (APP archive-capture backfill)

namesake.text: Poggio Bracciolini (1380-1459), who recovered lost classical texts from monastery archives

role: Finds permanent web-archive copies of 516 American Presidency Project pages that were saved only from the live site, without ever contacting that site.
inputs: APP index and documents from app-executive-orders
outputs: MIRROR_INDEX, MIRROR_DOCUMENTS, MIRROR_FRAGMENTS, MIRROR_FAILURES in its own folder

results.text: Run 2026-10-29T03:09:50Z (311 s): 516 seed ids, 456 already had a capture pointer and 456 were saved, 0 failed; 60 still without any capture (44 orders from 1933-1936, 14 from 2026, EO 1216, EO 12577).

history.text: Built as the archive-only phases of app_mirror.py with a host guard; README added, which also started the first run.

caveats: Restores custody (a reproducible hash) for APP text, not identity or originality; captures stay APP editorial transcriptions.
Output is not yet merged into app-executive-orders (merge is a manual app_mirror.py step, README:11-12).
60 of 516 pages have no capture, so those claims still fail custody.

name: Namier (same-person order finder)

namesake.text: Sir Lewis Namier, historian who studied the 18th-century House of Commons by collecting every record of every member (prosopography)

role: Reads each held order text once and lists other orders that name the same person, as leads for later-event checks on one-person orders.
inputs: X1 type table (civil-service waivers, retirement exemptions)
census orders whose title names a person

results.text: Run 2026-10-28T21:22:29Z: 2,231 subject orders, 1,935 with a parsable name (296 not); 557 with any hit; 243 with an unflagged later hit; 124 of those with no hit citing the number; 483 leads offered; 0 statuses changed, 0 legal conclusions.

Downstream test: nine serial retirement exemptions; seven claims passed the mechanical gate and a blind review upheld 7 of 7 genuine cards and caught the planted control, but kit.py complete found 0 eligible, 7 rejected_mechanical because APP page bytes were not held.

history.text: Job added with a claim-kit fix keeping number citations that carry no change verb.
Namier branch integrated with the other PRs.

caveats: A name match is a lead, not an identity authentication; two people share names (README:42-44).
An empty result covers only held texts and parsable names; it says nothing about the Official Register or agency records.
Nothing here decides a status, date, ending, identity or count.
Runs on frozen X1 and Lewis snapshots, not as same-run successors (README:73-77).

name: Shared identity and date helpers (eo_identity.py)
role: A shared code library that reads order numbers, loads the 14,972-order census and looks up every date or title any index gives an order.
outputs: loaded universe, dates, titles and saved texts for callers

history.text: Created for Lewis and Clark; used by Domesday the same day.
Named working-text grades kept; ProQuest scans dated from the WPA numbered list.

caveats: Read-only library; returns existing machine leads, not legal findings or identity authentication (docstring lines 8-10).
Also imported by pinakes-proquest-ingest and shepard-citations.
No measured result of its own is recorded; it is a dependency, not a research step.
